newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan's young OTC market bounds to new highs.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan's young OTC market bounds to new highs.

text.p: Both the index and daily turnover of Taiwan's fledgling over-the-counter securities exchange bounded to new highs on Monday on a rally led by financial shares.
The OTC index, echoing the main exchange's sizzling trade, ended up 5.82 points or 2.77 percent at 216.40, a record close.
Turnover hit T$10.42 billion, eclipsing the T$8.5 billion high set earlier in November.
In the major Taiwan Stock Exchange, the index hit a 22-month high of 6,938.87 points, up 1.41 percent from Saturday in a rally also led by the financial sector.
The over-the-counter exchange's daily turnover has rocketed since it inaugurated a new trading system in September 1995. Before that daily averages had languished in the T$1-$2 million range.
The new system requires securities brokerages to pay only deposits to the exchange before trading, rather than having to pay for stocks in full at the time of purchase.
There are 71 firms listed in the new exchange, which has said it hopes to reach 100 listings by the end of 1996.
